feasibility.verdict: partially feasible: single-column ELM can simulate fertilizer application, soil N cycling, and vertical nitrate leaching flux at the base of the soil column; the saturated-zone transport to wells and arrival concentrations require coupling to PFLOTRAN and cannot be resolved by ELM alone
answerable: Vertical nitrate leaching flux (NO3 export) below the crop root zone under fertilized corn/soybean management
Seasonal and interannual dynamics of soil mineral N, plant N uptake, and denitrification
Sensitivity of leaching to soil texture and fertilizer timing/rate
Recharge water flux delivering nitrate to the water table (drainage flux)
not_answerable: Lateral groundwater advection/dispersion from fields to specific drinking-water wells (requires 3D saturated-zone transport, out of scope for single-column ELM)
Actual arrival concentrations at named wells and travel times (requires PFLOTRAN reactive-transport with aquifer geometry and well locations)
Tile-drainage routing to streams (single-column has no lateral routing)

parsed.n_justification: Four columns span the dominant fertilized-agriculture soil textures and topographic positions of the Upper Iowa basin (loess-derived silt loams on uplands, silty clay loam footslopes, and coarser loam near alluvial/karst-recharge zones). This captures the primary controls on nitrate leaching (drainage rate, denitrification, water-holding capacity) while remaining a tractable site ensemble; each column supplies a bottom-boundary nitrate flux that can later drive PFLOTRAN.

columns.soil_texture: silty clay loam (poorly drained footslope, tile-drained)
sandy loam (thin soils over karst limestone, rapid recharge)

requires_capabilities: ELM active crop model (mizuroute-independent) with prognostic N cycle and managed fertilization (CROP on, e.g. corn/soybean rotation PFTs)
ELM nitrogen leaching diagnostics (SMIN_NO3_LEACHED at soil column base)
PFLOTRAN coupling (ELM-PFLOTRAN, PETSc) for saturated-zone reactive nitrate transport to wells
External well nitrate observations for evaluation of PFLOTRAN arrival concentrations
assumptions: GSWP3 (1980-2018) atmospheric forcing used as DATM CLMNCEP driver at each column location
Fertilizer rate/timing set to regional corn-soybean practice (~150-200 kg N/ha applied spring for corn) via ELM crop fertilization; adjust to local agronomic records if available
A multi-cycle spin-up (accelerated + regular, ~200+ years recycling forcing) precedes the 1980-2018 transient to equilibrate soil N and C pools
ELM provides the top boundary condition (recharge water flux and dissolved nitrate concentration) to PFLOTRAN; lateral aquifer transport and well arrival are computed in PFLOTRAN, not ELM
Karst rapid-recharge column approximates preferential flow via high hydraulic conductivity; explicit conduit flow is not represented in the 1D soil column
Well locations, aquifer properties, and hydraulic gradients must be supplied separately to the PFLOTRAN domain to estimate arrival concentrations
